entries.title: About NucleusFlow: Engineering Principles & Governance
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Project & Governance About NucleusFlow Built in London with memory-safe Rust, deterministic engineering, and zero telemetry. 1. Mission & Design Philosophy NucleusFlow (nucleusflow) was created to bridge the gap between monolithic static site generator binaries and low-level Markdown parsers. Engineering teams frequently need the same reliable content processing pipeline in two places: on the command line for static documentation builds, and inside Rust backend services for dynamic rendering and validation. NucleusFlow is guided by four core engineering invariants: Zero Unsafe Code (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]): Memory safety is non-negotiable when parsing untrusted Markdown, YAML frontmatter, and HTML templates. Composable Trait Boundaries: Content processing (Processor), template rendering (TemplateRenderer), and output generation (Generator) are cleanly separated so any stage can be swapped, mocked, or embedded independently. Deterministic Resource Budgets: Every stage enforces explicit byte caps (10 MB content, 64 KB metadata, 1 MB template, 100 MB cache) to guarantee predictable latency (~28.0 µs per page). Zero Telemetry: Neither the nucleusflow library/CLI nor the nucleusflow.com documentation portal makes outbound analytics, telemetry, or tracking requests. 2. Ecosystem Synergy NucleusFlow builds upon and integrates with open-source Rust crates maintained by Sebastien Rousseau: noyalib: Pure-Rust, memory-safe YAML 1.2 parser powering NucleusFlow's frontmatter extraction. dtt: Date, time, and timezone utilities for structured build timestamps. ssg: The Static Site Generator compiling this documentation portal (nucleusflow.com). Skeletonic CSS: Lightweight, WCAG 2.2 Level AAA CSS layout foundation. 3. Governance & Maintainer NucleusFlow is authored and maintained by Sebastien Rousseau in London, United Kingdom. All architectural changes, releases, and security advisories are managed transparently on GitHub: Core Rust Library & CLI: github.com/sebastienrousseau/nucleusflow Documentation Portal: github.com/sebastienrousseau/nucleusflow.github.io Crates.io Package: crates.io/crates/nucleusflow API Documentation: docs.rs/nucleusflow

entries.title: API & CLI Reference: NucleusFlow Rust Crate & Command-Line Interface
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Developer Reference API & CLI Reference Complete Rust library types, traits, configuration builders, and CLI subcommands. 1. Crate Overview & Re-Exports (nucleusflow) The root nucleusflow module re-exports the primary pipeline types so applications can import them directly from nucleusflow::*: Symbol Module Path Description NucleusFlow nucleusflow::NucleusFlow Top-level pipeline orchestrator connecting content processing, template rendering, and HTML generation NucleusFlowConfig nucleusflow::NucleusFlowConfig Directory configuration (content_dir, output_dir, template_dir) for NucleusFlow ContentProcessor nucleusflow::processors::markdown::MarkdownProcessor Stage 1 CommonMark + GFM + YAML 1.2 frontmatter processor HandlebarsRenderer nucleusflow::template::HtmlTemplateRenderer Stage 2 thread-safe cached Handlebars template renderer HtmlGenerator nucleusflow::generators::html::HtmlOutputGenerator Stage 3 HTML5 validator, <meta> injector, and minifier FileContentProcessor nucleusflow::process::FileContentProcessor File-oriented content processor with path sanitization and extension checks TemplateRenderer nucleusflow::template::TemplateRenderer Trait for rendering named templates with JSON context values ConfigBuilder nucleusflow::core::config::ConfigBuilder Builder for multi-profile TOML and environment configuration ProcessingError nucleusflow::core::error::ProcessingError Unified error enum for all pipeline stages Full generated Rustdoc is available on docs.rs/nucleusflow. 2. Stage 1: Content Processing (nucleusflow::processors::markdown) MarkdownProcessor (re-exported as ContentProcessor) use nucleusflow::ContentProcessor; use nucleusflow::core::traits::Processor; let processor = ContentProcessor::new() .with_toc() .with_sanitization() .with_custom_Metadata("site_name".to_string(), "NucleusFlow".to_string()); let html = processor.process("# Heading\n\nParagraph text.")?; Method Signature Behavior new() pub fn new() -> Self Creates a processor with GFM tables, footnotes, and strikethrough enabled with_toc() pub fn with_toc(self) -> Self Enables automatic <nav class="toc"> generation from document headings with_sanitization() pub fn with_sanitization(self) -> Self Enables HTML tag allowlist (ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS) and XSS pattern blocking with_options(opts) pub fn with_options(self, options: Options) -> Self Customizes pulldown_cmark::Options bitflags with_custom_Metadata(k, v) pub fn with_custom_Metadata(self, key: String, value: String) -> Self Attaches custom metadata key-value pairs process(&self, input) fn process(&self, input: &str) -> Result<String, ProcessingError> Validates size (<= 10 MB), extracts YAML frontmatter, renders Markdown, and sanitizes output 3. Stage 2: Template Rendering (nucleusflow::template) HtmlTemplateRenderer (re-exported as HandlebarsRenderer) use nucleusflow:: {HandlebarsRenderer, TemplateRenderer}; use nucleusflow::template::UppercaseHelper; use serde_json::json; let renderer = HandlebarsRenderer::new() .with_template_dir("templates") .with_strict_mode() .with_helper("upper".to_string(), Box::new(UppercaseHelper)); renderer.load_templates()?; let rendered = renderer.render("page", &json!({ "title": "API Guide" }))?; Method Signature Behavior new() pub fn new() -> Self Initializes an Arc<RwLock<Handlebars>> registry with UppercaseHelper registered with_template_dir(dir) pub fn with_template_dir<P: Into<PathBuf>>(self, dir: P) -> Self Sets the directory used by load_templates() to scan .hbs files with_partial(name, content) pub fn with_partial(self, name: String, content: String) -> Result<Self, ProcessingError> Validates and registers a named Handlebars partial with_helper(name, helper) pub fn with_helper(self, name: String, helper: Box<dyn TemplateHelper>) -> Self Registers a custom TemplateHelper implementation with_strict_mode() pub fn with_strict_mode(self) -> Self Requires all referenced template variables to exist in the context JSON load_templates(&self) pub fn load_templates(&self) -> Result<(), ProcessingError> Recursively loads all .hbs files from template_dir into the cache register_template(&mut self, name, tpl) fn register_template(&mut self, name: &str, template: &str) -> Result<(), ProcessingError> Validates brace balance and compiles a template into the registry render(&self, name, data) fn render(&self, template_name: &str, data: &Value) -> Result<String, ProcessingError> Renders a cached template with a serde_json::Value context 4. Stage 3: Output Generation (nucleusflow::generators::html) HtmlOutputGenerator (re-exported as HtmlGenerator) use std::collections::HashMap; use nucleusflow::HtmlGenerator; use nucleusflow::core::traits::Generator; let mut meta = HashMap::new(); meta.insert("author".to_string(), "Sebastien Rousseau".to_string()); let generator = HtmlGenerator::new() .with_minification() .with_meta_tags(meta) .with_asset_dir("static"); let output = generator.generate("<!DOCTYPE

entries.title: Pipeline Architecture: Three-Stage Trait Design & Thread Safety
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System System Design Three-Stage Pipeline Architecture How NucleusFlow processes Markdown, templates, and HTML5 with deterministic concurrency. 1. End-to-End Execution Flow NucleusFlow decouples static site generation into three composable stages coordinated by NucleusFlow: +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Configuration & CLI Layer | | ConfigBuilder (nucleusflow.toml + NUCLEUSFLOW_* env) / clap 4.5 CLI | +------------------------------------+------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Stage 1: ContentProcessor (Processor) | | 1. Enforce 10 MB input cap & path traversal sanitization | | 2. Extract YAML 1.2 frontmatter (noyalib 0.0.58) | | 3. Parse CommonMark + GFM tables/footnotes (pulldown-cmark 0.13.5) | | 4. Synthesize <nav class="toc"> & Schema.org JSON-LD metadata | | 5. Enforce ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS & block XSS attribute/URI patterns | +------------------------------------+------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Stage 2: HandlebarsRenderer (TemplateRenderer) | | 1. Validate balanced braces & strict-mode context variables | | 2. Read compiled .hbs templates from Arc<parking_lot::RwLock<...>> | | 3. Evaluate partials and custom TemplateHelper implementations | +------------------------------------+------------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Stage 3: HtmlGenerator (Generator) | | 1. Verify HTML5 structural tag balance (void & optional-close aware) | | 2. Inject HTML-escaped <meta> tags into <head> | | 3. Minify HTML/CSS/JS (minify-html 0.18.1) or pretty-print | | 4. Copy cached static assets & write output files (0o644 permissions) | +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ 2. Crate Module Layout The nucleusflow workspace is organized into focused modules with strict complexity ceilings (<= 10 cyclomatic complexity, <= 15 cognitive complexity per function): Source File Responsibility src/lib.rs Top-level NucleusFlow orchestrator, NucleusFlowConfig, crate-level #![forbid(unsafe_code)], and public re-exports src/main.rs Binary entrypoint initializing structured logging (dtt + log) and dispatching CLI subcommands src/cli.rs Declarative clap 4.5 command-line parser (new, build, serve) and argument validation src/core/config.rs Config, ConfigBuilder, Profile, ContentConfig, TemplateConfig, OutputConfig, and safe environment variable merging src/core/traits.rs Core abstraction traits (Processor, Transform, Generator, Validator, ProcessingContext, Shareable) src/core/error.rs Structured ProcessingError enum (thiserror 2.0) covering all validation, parsing, template, and I/O failures src/process.rs FileContentProcessor with path sanitization (sanitize_path), file extension allowlists, and ProcessError src/processors/markdown.rs MarkdownProcessor implementing CommonMark + GFM parsing, YAML frontmatter extraction, TOC generation, and HTML sanitization src/template.rs HtmlTemplateRenderer wrapping handlebars::Handlebars in Arc<parking_lot::RwLock<...>>, partial management, and UppercaseHelper src/generators/html.rs HtmlOutputGenerator implementing HTML5 tag balance verification, <meta> injection, minify-html integration, and asset caching 3. Concurrency & parking_lot::RwLock Caching Static site builds are heavily read-biased: templates and configuration are compiled once at startup and read concurrently across hundreds or thousands of content pages. Zero Poisoning Overhead: NucleusFlow uses parking_lot::RwLock (0.13) rather than std::sync::RwLock, avoiding lock poisoning overhead and providing compact, fast uncontended read locks. Blanket Shareable Trait: Every component implementing Send + Sync + 'static automatically gains .into_shared(), wrapping the instance in Arc<RwLock<Self>> for multi-threaded pipeline execution. Async Runtime Compatibility: ConfigBuilder supports asynchronous reload tasks on tokio (1.47) while keeping the core parsing and rendering path synchronous and allocation-lean. 4. Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) All load-bearing architectural invariants in the nucleusflow repository are documented under docs/adr/: ADR Title Status Core Invariant ADR-0001 Zero Unsafe Rust Policy Accepted Enforces #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate roots (src/lib.rs and src/main.rs) and audits dependencies via cargo-deny. ADR-0002 Deterministic Rendering Pipeline Accepted Separates content parsing, template evaluation, and HTML generation behind deterministic traits synchronized with parking_lot::RwLock. ADR-0003 Path Traversal Rejection Accepted Rejects .., null bytes, and leading slashes in sanitize_path before any filesystem read or write, verified by proptest fuzzing.

entries.title: Performance Benchmarks: Sub-30 Microsecond Rust Content Pipeline
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Performance Engineering Sub-30 Microsecond Benchmarks Reproducible Criterion 0.8 latency measurements and ecosystem comparison. 1. Benchmark Methodology & Hardware Baseline All performance numbers reported for NucleusFlow are measured using Criterion.rs (criterion = "0.8") in /benches/processing_benchmark.rs and can be reproduced locally on any machine. Hardware: Apple Silicon (M4, macOS) Toolchain: rustc 1.89.0 (2021 Edition), --release profile (opt-level = 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1) Harness: cargo bench --bench processing_benchmark 2. Stage-by-Stage Micro-Benchmarks Benchmark Suite Operation Median Time Throughput Equivalent markdown_processing Parse CommonMark + GFM + extract YAML 1.2 frontmatter ~4.2 µs ~238,000 docs / sec (single core) template_rendering Evaluate compiled Handlebars layout with nested partials ~12.5 µs ~80,000 renders / sec (single core) html_minification Validate HTML5 tags & collapse whitespace (minify-html) ~8.1 µs ~123,000 pages / sec (single core) single_page_pipeline End-to-end read, parse, render, minify, and write ~28.0 µs ~35,700 pages / sec (single core) At ~28.0 µs per page on a single thread, a 1,000-page documentation portal processes through the entire Markdown, Handlebars, and HTML5 minification pipeline in ~28 milliseconds. 3. Ecosystem Comparison How NucleusFlow compares against established static site generators and content engines: Feature / Dimension NucleusFlow (v0.0.11) Zola Hugo Eleventy (11ty) Implementation Language Rust (1.89.0+) Rust Go JavaScript (Node.js) Memory Safety Guarantee #![forbid(unsafe_code)] Standard Rust Go GC V8 GC Usage Model Library Crate + CLI Binary CLI Binary only CLI Binary only Node CLI / NPM package Template Engine Handlebars (.hbs) Tera (.html) Go html/template Liquid / Nunjucks / Hbs Frontmatter Parser YAML 1.2 (noyalib) TOML (+++) / YAML YAML / TOML / JSON YAML / JSON / JS Built-in HTML Sanitizer Yes (ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS + XSS filter) No Partial Via external plugins Built-in HTML5 Minifier Yes (minify-html in ~8.1 µs) Yes Yes Via external plugins Bounded DoS Budgets Explicit content, template & cache caps Unbounded Unbounded Unbounded 4. Reproducing Benchmarks Locally Clone the core library repository and run the Criterion benchmark suite: git clone https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/nucleusflow.git cd nucleusflow cargo bench --bench processing_benchmark HTML latency distribution plots and regression comparisons are written automatically to target/criterion/report/index.html.

entries.title: Contributing to NucleusFlow: Workflow, Quality Gates & Commit Standards
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Open Source Contributing to NucleusFlow Engineering standards, verification gates, and pull request discipline. 1. Development Workflow We welcome contributions to both the core Rust repository and the documentation portal. Fork & Branch: Create a feature branch targeting the next patch iteration (feat/vX.Y.Z). Code Quality & Complexity Ceilings: Zero unsafe blocks (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]). Cyclomatic complexity <= 10 per function; cognitive complexity <= 15 per function. Maximum 60 lines of code per function and 500 lines per file. SPDX Headers: Every source file must carry SPDX-FileCopyrightText and SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR MIT headers. 2. Running Local Quality Gates Core Rust Library (nucleusflow) cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings cargo test --all-targets --all-features Documentation Website (nucleusflow.github.io) # Compile with ssg 0.0.69 and run all lint, test, and WCAG AAA audit suites make verify 3. Commit & Pull Request Conventions Conventional Commits: <type>: <subject> (maximum 50 characters, imperative mood; body wrapped at 72 characters). Signed Commits: Sign commits with SSH/GPG (git commit -S -s). Dual Licensing: All contributions are provided under the repository's dual Apache-2.0 OR MIT license.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) | NucleusFlow
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Questions & Answers Frequently Asked Questions Technical guidance on NucleusFlow's three-stage Rust architecture, supported formats, microsecond benchmarks, and dual licensing. All Questions 8 Architecture & API 3 Formats & Templates 3 Security & Licensing 2 Showing 8 of 8 questions Expand all Architecture Can I use NucleusFlow as a Rust library inside my own application, or is it only a CLI? Both. Unlike monolithic static site binaries such as Hugo or Zola, NucleusFlow is published on Crates.io as both a library crate (nucleusflow) and a CLI binary. You can import ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, HtmlGenerator, or the top-level NucleusFlow orchestrator directly into your Rust services. Toolchain What is the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)? NucleusFlow requires Rust 1.89.0 or newer (2021 Edition). This floor is verified in CI and enforced at build time by Cargo.toml and build.rs. Concurrency Is NucleusFlow thread-safe for concurrent rendering? Yes. Every core stage implements Send + Sync and the blanket Shareable trait (.into_shared()), wrapping instances in Arc<parking_lot::RwLock<Self>> so compiled Handlebars templates and assets can be shared safely across worker threads. Markdown Which Markdown extensions and frontmatter formats are supported? MarkdownProcessor parses CommonMark plus GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM tables, footnotes, and strikethrough) via pulldown-cmark 0.13.5, and extracts --- fenced YAML 1.2 frontmatter via noyalib 0.0.58. Templating Why does NucleusFlow use Handlebars (.hbs) templates? Handlebars enforces logic-less templates with clear separation between presentation layouts and Rust business logic, while supporting partials, custom TemplateHelper functions, and strict variable checking via the battle-tested handlebars 6.2 crate. HTML5 Does NucleusFlow validate and minify HTML5 output automatically? Yes. HtmlGenerator verifies structural HTML5 tag balance (accounting for void elements like img and meta as well as optional-closing elements like p and li) and minifies HTML, inline CSS, and inline JS in ~8.1 µs using minify-html 0.18.1. Safety Does NucleusFlow contain any unsafe Rust code? No. Both the library crate and CLI binary enforce #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate root per ADR-0001. Licensing How is NucleusFlow licensed? NucleusFlow and its documentation are dual-licensed under your choice of the Apache License, Version 2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE) or the MIT License (LICENSE-MIT). No matching questions found Try searching for broader terms such as “Handlebars”, “YAML”, “MSRV”, or “CLI”. Reset search & filters Have a question not listed here? Explore the documentation guides, open an issue on GitHub, or contact the maintainer directly. Getting Started Guide GitHub Issues Contact Support

entries.title: Supported Formats: CommonMark, GFM, YAML 1.2, Handlebars & HTML5
entries.content:
Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Format Specifications Supported Content, Template & Config Formats Input, template, configuration, and output formats across the three-stage pipeline. Format Support Matrix NucleusFlow processes structured text and templates through strict, memory-safe Rust parsers with deterministic resource budgets: Format Category Specification / Syntax Underlying Crate Default Size Budget Stage Markdown Content CommonMark + GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 10 MB (MAX_CONTENT_SIZE) Stage 1 (MarkdownProcessor) Document Frontmatter YAML 1.2 (--- fenced header block) noyalib 0.0.58 64 KB (max_metadata_size) Stage 1 (MarkdownProcessor) Layout Templates Handlebars (.hbs) with partials & helpers handlebars 6.2 1 MB (max_template_size) Stage 2 (HandlebarsRenderer) Pipeline Configuration TOML (nucleusflow.toml) & Env Overrides toml 0.9.5 + serde 1.0 1 MB (MAX_CONFIG_SIZE) Core (ConfigBuilder) Generated Markup HTML5 + Schema.org JSON-LD + tags minify-html 0.18.1 100 MB (max_output_size) Stage 3 (HtmlGenerator) 1. CommonMark & GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) MarkdownProcessor uses pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 with GFM extensions enabled by default: GFM Tables (ENABLE_TABLES): Pipe-delimited tables with column alignment (:---, :---:, ---:). Footnotes (ENABLE_FOOTNOTES): Inline footnote references ([^1]) and bottom definition blocks. Strikethrough (ENABLE_STRIKETHROUGH): Double-tilde (~~deleted~~) inline formatting. Automated Table of Contents (with_toc()): Extracts heading hierarchies (h1 through h6), generates URL-safe slugs, and prepends a semantic
    ...
block. HTML Allowlist Sanitization (with_sanitization()): Inspects inline HTML tags against ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS (p, div, span, h1..h6, ul, ol, li, a, img, code, pre, blockquote, em, strong, del, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, sup, sub, br, hr) and rejects suspicious patterns ( block with @context: "https://schema.org" and @type: "Article" when rendered through MarkdownProcessor. 3. Handlebars Templates (.hbs) HandlebarsRenderer (HtmlTemplateRenderer) compiles .hbs templates using handlebars 6.2 and caches compiled templates inside an Arc>: Context Variables: Standard page fields (title, description, content, author, date) and custom metadata key-value pairs. Reusable Partials (with_partial): Register shared layout components such as headers, footers, and navigation menus. Custom Helpers (with_helper / TemplateHelper trait): Implement the TemplateHelper trait (fn execute(&self, args: &[Value]) -> Result) or use the built-in UppercaseHelper. Strict Mode (with_strict_mode): Verifies that every {{variable}} referenced in the template exists in the rendering context before execution, returning ProcessingError::TemplateDataError if any required key is missing. Balanced Brace Verification: Pre-validates template syntax for matching {{ and }} delimiters before invoking the compiler. 4. HTML5 Output & Minification HtmlGenerator (HtmlOutputGenerator) transforms rendered template output into production-ready HTML5 files: HTML5 Structural Validation: Validates tag nesting and closing order while properly recognizing HTML5 void elements (area, base, br, col, embed, hr, img, input, link, meta, param, source, track, wbr) and optional-closing elements (p, dt, dd, li, option, thead, th, tbody, tr, td, tfoot, colgroup). Escaped Injection (with_meta_tags): Escapes &, <, >, ", and ' in metadata keys and values and injects into . Sub-10 µs Minification (with_minification): Uses minify-html 0.18.1 to minify HTML, inline CSS (minify_css: true), and inline JavaScript (minify_js: true) while preserving closing tags for strict validator compatibility. Pretty-Printing (without_minification): Indents nested HTML elements cleanly for local debugging and snapshot inspection. 5. Multi-Environment Configuration (nucleusflow.toml) ConfigBuilder loads TOML configuration files, validates numerical bounds, and optionally applies environment variable overrides: profile = "production" [content] max_content_size = 10485760 max_metadata_size = 65536 allowed_extensions = ["md", "markdown"] validate_markdown = true allow_html = false [templates] max_template_size =

entries.title: Getting Started with NucleusFlow: Rust CLI & Library Quickstart
entries.content:
Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Quickstart Guide Getting Started with NucleusFlow Install the standalone CLI or embed the Rust crate in under five minutes. 1. Prerequisites & Toolchain Floor NucleusFlow requires Rust 1.89.0 or later (2021 Edition). The Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) is enforced at compile time via Cargo.toml (rust-version = "1.89.0") and build.rs. 2. Installation As a Rust Library Dependency Add nucleusflow to your project's Cargo.toml: [dependencies] nucleusflow = "0.0.11" Or run cargo add: cargo add nucleusflow As a Standalone Command-Line Binary Install the nucleusflow CLI directly from Crates.io: cargo install nucleusflow --locked System Package Managers & Containers NucleusFlow ships native packaging definitions across major operating systems in the upstream repository (pkg/): Channel Command / Manifest Notes Cargo cargo install nucleusflow --locked Builds from source with Rust 1.89.0+ Homebrew brew install pkg/brew/nucleusflow.rb macOS & Linux formula Nix Flakes nix run github:sebastienrousseau/nucleusflow Reproducible flake (pkg/nix/flake.nix) Arch Linux (AUR) makepkg -si in pkg/aur/ Builds from signed release tarball Debian / Ubuntu dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b Includes binary, manpage nucleusflow.1, completions Fedora / RHEL rpmbuild -ba pkg/rpm/nucleusflow.spec RPM spec with manpage and shell completions GNU Make make install PREFIX=/usr/local Installs binary, manpage, and bash/zsh/fish/pwsh completions 3. CLI Quick Start Step 1: Scaffold a New Site Create a new project directory using one of the built-in starter templates (blog, docs, or portfolio): nucleusflow new my-docs --template docs cd my-docs This creates a standard directory layout with content/, templates/, public/, and nucleusflow.toml. Step 2: Build the Static Site Compile all Markdown files in content/ through your Handlebars layouts in templates/ and write minified HTML5 to public/: nucleusflow build \ --content-dir content \ --output-dir public \ --template-dir templates \ --minify \ --config nucleusflow.toml Step 3: Preview Locally with Live Watch Start the local development server on port 3000 with automatic file watching: nucleusflow serve --port 3000 --watch --dir public 4. Rust Library Quick Start End-to-End Pipeline (NucleusFlow) Combine ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, and HtmlGenerator behind the top-level NucleusFlow orchestrator: use nucleusflow::{ ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, HtmlGenerator, NucleusFlow, NucleusFlowConfig, }; fn main() -> Result<(), Box> { // 1. Configure content, output, and template directories let config = NucleusFlowConfig::new("content", "public", "templates"); // 2. Configure Stage 1 (Markdown + YAML frontmatter + TOC + sanitization) let content_processor = ContentProcessor::new() .with_toc() .with_sanitization(); // 3. Configure Stage 2 (Handlebars templates + strict variable checking) let template_renderer = HandlebarsRenderer::new() .with_strict_mode(); // 4. Configure Stage 3 (HTML5 tag balance check + minification) let output_generator = HtmlGenerator::new() .with_minification() .with_asset_dir("static"); // 5. entries.title: NucleusFlow: Fast, Secure Rust Static Site Generator & Content Pipeline
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Rust Content Processing · Open SourceCompile static pages in microseconds.Zero unsafe code. Zero telemetry.An open-source, high-throughput static site generator and content processing pipeline engineered in pure memory-safe Rust. Converts CommonMark + GFM with YAML 1.2 frontmatter and cached Handlebars templates into validated, minified HTML5 in ~28.0 µs per page as both an embeddable crate and standalone CLI.Install CLI & Crate Explore Supported Formats#![forbid(unsafe_code)] Rust Core~28.0 µs Single-Page PipelineLibrary Crate + Standalone CLI~28.0 µs / Page End-to-end read, Markdown parse, Handlebars render, HTML5 minification, and write.~4.2 µs Markdown + YAML CommonMark + GFM tables/footnotes (`pulldown-cmark`) and YAML 1.2 frontmatter (`noyalib`).~12.5 µs Template Render Thread-safe `parking_lot::RwLock` compiled Handlebars template cache with partials and helpers.Zero Unsafe Code Crate-wide `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, HTML allowlist sanitization, and path traversal rejection. Composable Rust ArchitectureEmbeddable Pipeline for Modern EngineeringStop maintaining separate Markdown parsers for backend services and monolithic binaries for documentation portals. Share the exact same trait-driven Rust pipeline across your CLI builds, CI/CD jobs, and web microservices.View Production Workflows ↗Engine ArchitectureEngineered for deterministic safety.Three-stage trait pipeline combining memory-safe Rust execution, bounded DoS budgets, and dual Apache-2.0 or MIT licensing.01ContentProcessor (Stage 1)Extracts YAML 1.2 frontmatter via noyalib, parses CommonMark + GFM tables, footnotes, and strikethrough via pulldown-cmark, generates semantic TOC navigation, and enforces an explicit HTML tag allowlist.02HandlebarsRenderer (Stage 2)Compiles and caches .hbs templates in a thread-safe parking_lot::RwLock registry. Supports nested partials, custom TemplateHelper implementations, balanced-brace checks, and strict variable validation.03HtmlGenerator (Stage 3)Verifies HTML5 structural tag balance across void and optional-close elements, injects escaped meta tags into head, minifies HTML/CSS/JS in ~8.1 µs via minify-html, and manages static asset caching.The Processing PipelineFrom Markdown source to minified HTML5.1ExtractValidate 10 MB content budgets, sanitize file paths, and parse YAML 1.2 frontmatter into Schema.org JSON-LD metadata.noyalib 0.0.58 frontmatter engine2ParseTransform CommonMark + GFM tables, footnotes, and strikethrough into sanitized HTML with automated Table of Contents.~4.2 µs pulldown-cmark 0.13.53RenderEvaluate compiled .hbs Handlebars layouts, partials, and custom helpers from the concurrent RwLock cache.~12.5 µs handlebars 6.2 render4MinifyVerify HTML5 tag balance, inject escaped meta tags, and collapse HTML, inline CSS, and JS whitespace.~8.1 µs minify-html 0.18.1 High-Performance PipelineDeterministic Execution at Enterprise ScaleEngineered for documentation portals and backend services requiring bounded memory budgets, lock-free read concurrency, and zero unsafe blocks.View Architecture Blueprint ↗Developer QuickstartInstall via Cargo, Homebrew, or Nix in SecondsRun as a standalone CLI binary to scaffold, build, and live-serve static sites, or add the crate to your Cargo.toml to embed the pipeline in Rust.Full Documentation → API & CLI Reference bash - nucleusflow# 1. Install standalone CLI and Rust crate (v0.0.11)$cargo install nucleusflow --locked$nucleusflow new docs-portal --template docs# 2. Compile CommonMark + Handlebars with HTML5 minification$nucleusflow build --content-dir content --output-dir public --minify# 3. Deterministic pipeline output (~28.0 µs / page){ "status": "COMPLETED", "latency_us": 28.0, "unsafe_blocks": 0 }Defense-in-Depth SecurityMemory-safe Rust with strict input boundaries.NucleusFlow enforces #![forbid(unsafe_code)] across every module (ADR-0001), rejects path traversal via property-tested sanitize_path (ADR-0003), sanitizes HTML against an explicit tag allowlist, and caps input budgets with zero outbound network calls.Read Security Architecture ↓Clear AnswersFrequently Asked QuestionsCan I use NucleusFlow as a Rust library as well as a CLI binary?Yes. Unlike monolithic static site binaries such as Hugo or Zola, NucleusFlow is published on Crates.io as both a library crate (nucleusflow) and a standalone CLI binary. You can embed ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, HtmlGenerator, or the NucleusFlow orchestrator directly inside your Rust services.Which Markdown, frontmatter, and template formats are supported?NucleusFlow parses CommonMark plus GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, footnotes, strikethrough) via pulldown-cmark 0.13.5, extracts YAML 1.2 frontmatter via noyalib 0.0.58, compiles Handlebars (.hbs) templates via handlebars 6.2, and minifies HTML5 via minify-html 0.18.1.What is the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)?NucleusFlow requires Rust 1.89.0 or newer (2021 Edition). entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Documentation Stack Made with SSG & Skeletonic CSS How this documentation portal is compiled, fingerprinted, and audited. Built with Rust ssg (v0.0.69) & Skeletonic CSS The nucleusflow.com documentation portal is compiled using the Static Site Generator (ssg) (v0.0.69) and styled with Skeletonic CSS (Visage design system). Build & Verification Pipeline Content & Templates: Markdown articles in _posts/*.md are rendered into _layouts/*.html templates. Asset Fingerprinting & SRI: ssg hashes stylesheets and scripts (styles.<hash>.css, main.<hash>.js) and injects sha384- Subresource Integrity (SRI) attributes. Syndication & Discovery: Automatically emits sitemap.xml, rss.xml, atom.xml, feed.json, search-index.json, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and CycloneDX SBOM (sbom.cdx.json). 10-Pillar Quality Gate: Every commit is verified against WCAG 2.2 Level AAA contrast ratios, HTML5 structural validation, Hypothesis property tests, and SPDX license compliance.
headings: Built with Rust ssg (v0.0.69) & Skeletonic CSS

entries.title: Privacy Policy: Zero Telemetry & Zero Cookies | NucleusFlow
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Zero Telemetry Privacy Policy Zero tracking, zero analytics cookies, and 100% offline-capable software. 1. Zero Telemetry in nucleusflow Library & CLI The nucleusflow Rust library crate and command-line binary operate 100% locally on your files. They contain zero telemetry, zero crash-reporting beacons, and zero outbound network requests during project scaffolding (new) or static site compilation (build). 2. Zero Tracking on nucleusflow.com This documentation website (https://nucleusflow.com) is a purely static site compiled with ssg and hosted on GitHub Pages: No Cookies: We do not set tracking, advertising, or session cookies. No Third-Party Analytics: We do not embed Google Analytics, Meta pixels, or third-party behavioral scripts. Local Theme Preference Only: Your selected colour theme (light, dark, or system) is stored exclusively in your browser's local localStorage under the key visage-theme-mode and is never transmitted over the network. Client-Side Search: Site search queries run entirely in-browser against the static /search-index.json file. Contact Form: If you voluntarily submit a message via the Contact page, the fields you enter (name, email, message) are processed via Formspree solely to deliver your inquiry to the maintainer.
headings: 1. Zero Telemetry in nucleusflow Library & CLI

entries.title: Security & Memory Safety: Zero Unsafe Rust & XSS Defense
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Defense in Depth Security & Memory-Safe Rust Crate-wide #![forbid(unsafe_code)], path traversal prevention, and HTML sanitization. 1. Crate-Wide #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (ADR-0001) Both src/lib.rs and src/main.rs declare #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate root. Any attempt to introduce an unsafe block fails compilation immediately. Combined with cargo-deny and cargo-audit in CI, NucleusFlow eliminates buffer overflows, use-after-free bugs, and undefined memory behavior across its content processing pipeline. 2. Path Traversal Prevention (ADR-0003) Static site generators read content files, templates, and static assets from disk and mirror directory structures into output trees. NucleusFlow enforces strict path validation at every I/O boundary: FileContentProcessor (sanitize_path): Rejects any path containing .. parent traversal segments, null bytes (\0), or leading / root escapes before opening a file, returning ProcessError::InvalidInput. HtmlGenerator::copy_assets_to: Verifies that every cached relative asset path contains no .. components before creating subdirectories or writing output files. Property-Based Fuzzing (proptest 1.6): Path sanitization invariants are continuously fuzz-tested against arbitrary string inputs in the test suite. 3. HTML Allowlist Sanitization & XSS Prevention When ContentProcessor::new().with_sanitization() is active, MarkdownProcessor enforces a two-layer filter on rendered HTML: Tag Allowlist (ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS): Only permits p, div, span, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, a, img, code, pre, blockquote, em, strong, del, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, sup, sub, br, and hr. Any unapproved tag (such as <script>, <iframe>, <object>, <embed>, <form>, or <style>) triggers ProcessingError::HtmlSanitizationError. Suspicious Pattern Blocker: Scans for javascript:, data:, vbscript:, onclick, onerror, onload, and eval(, blocking dangerous URI schemes and inline event handlers. Escaped <meta> Injection: HtmlGenerator escapes &, <, >, ", and ' in all <meta> tag names and values before inserting them into <head>. 4. Deterministic Denial-of-Service (DoS) Budgets Every stage enforces explicit upper bounds so untrusted or malformed files cannot exhaust process memory: Resource Budget Default Limit Enforced By Markdown Content Size 10 MB (10,485,760 bytes) MarkdownProcessor::MAX_CONTENT_SIZE & ContentConfig Frontmatter Metadata Size 64 KB (65,536 bytes) ContentConfig::max_metadata_size Template File Size 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes) TemplateConfig::max_template_size Template Cache Memory 100 MB (104,857,600 bytes) TemplateConfig::max_cache_size Configuration File Size 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes) ConfigBuilder::MAX_CONFIG_SIZE Generated Output Size 100 MB (104,857,600 bytes) OutputConfig::max_output_size Environment Variable Filter Blocks PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL ConfigBuilder::is_safe_env_var 5. Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (RFC 9116) Report suspected vulnerabilities privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by email to sebastian.rousseau@gmail.com. Machine-readable disclosure metadata is published at /.well-known/security.txt. Initial acknowledgement is provided within 48 hours.

entries.title: Use Cases: Documentation Portals, Embedded Pipelines & CI/CD Publishing
entries.content: Skip to main content NucleusFlow Menu Change colour theme System Production Workflows Real-World Use Cases & Integration Patterns How engineering teams deploy NucleusFlow across web portals and backend services. 1. Technical Documentation Portals & Developer Hubs Engineering organizations use the nucleusflow CLI (--template docs) to compile multi-version product manuals, ADR catalogs, and API guides with zero runtime JavaScript dependencies. Automated Table of Contents (with_toc): Every documentation page automatically receives a semantic <nav class="toc"> anchor tree derived from h1..h6 headings. Schema.org JSON-LD Structured Data: YAML 1.2 frontmatter fields are automatically emitted as <script type="application/ld+json"> metadata for search engine and LLM indexing. Sub-30 µs Page Compilation: Rebuild hundreds of documentation pages in milliseconds during local nucleusflow serve --watch editing sessions. 2. Embedded Content Pipelines in Rust Web Services Because NucleusFlow is architected as a library crate (nucleusflow = "0.0.11") first and a CLI second, Rust web servers (Axum, Actix-Web, Tower) can embed ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, and HtmlGenerator directly in-process: use std::sync::Arc; use parking_lot::RwLock; use nucleusflow::{ContentProcessor, HandlebarsRenderer, HtmlGenerator}; use nucleusflow::core::traits::Shareable; pub struct ContentEngine { pub processor: Arc<RwLock<ContentProcessor>>, pub renderer: Arc<RwLock<HandlebarsRenderer>>, pub generator: Arc<RwLock<HtmlGenerator>>, } impl ContentEngine { pub fn new() -> Self { Self { processor: ContentProcessor::new().with_toc().with_sanitization().into_shared(), renderer: HandlebarsRenderer::new().with_strict_mode().into_shared(), generator: HtmlGenerator::new().with_minification().into_shared(), } } } 3. Sanitized User-Submitted Markdown Rendering Platforms that accept Markdown from external contributors, webhooks, or CMS editors require strict protection against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and resource exhaustion: Explicit Tag Allowlist: ContentProcessor::new().with_sanitization() restricts inline HTML to ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS (p, div, span, h1..h6, ul, ol, li, a, img, code, pre, blockquote, em, strong, del, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, sup, sub, br, hr). Active Pattern Blocking: Rejects javascript:, data:, vbscript:, inline event handlers (onclick, onerror, onload), and eval( expressions with ProcessingError::HtmlSanitizationError. 10 MB Input Ceiling: Prevents denial-of-service memory spikes before invoking the parser. 4. High-Speed CI/CD Static Publishing & Changelogs Run nucleusflow build --minify inside ephemeral CI runners or distroless containers to compile release notes, security advisories, and compliance reports into static HTML5 artifacts with 0o644 permissions and verified tag balance.
headings: 2. Embedded Content Pipelines in Rust Web Services
